title: Conditional and restrictive connectors
schema: english-prompt -> learner types German -> Reveal/Hide answer shows reference + speaker

exercises.english: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
exercises.german: Wenn es morgen regnet, bleiben wir zu Hause.
exercises.why: Real future condition: the wenn-clause is verb-final (regnet) and the main clause verb follows in position II.

exercises.english: When I moved to Berlin in 2019, I knew nobody there.
exercises.german: Als ich 2019 nach Berlin zog, kannte ich dort niemanden.
exercises.why: als marks a single completed event in the past, so it is the correct connector and not wenn.

exercises.english: If the train is cancelled, I will take the bus.
exercises.german: Falls der Zug ausfällt, nehme ich den Bus.
exercises.why: falls is a formal variant of wenn and signals a contingency rather than an expectation.

exercises.english: Whenever my sister calls, the phone stays on silent.
exercises.german: Immer wenn meine Schwester anruft, läuft das Handy stumm.
exercises.why: Immer wenn expresses recurrence; the clause closes with the separable verb anruft.

exercises.english: If you have questions, please contact the management.
exercises.german: Wenn Sie Fragen haben, wenden Sie sich bitte an die Leitung.
exercises.why: Formal Sie plus the verb-first imperative in the main clause; wenn-clause stays verb-final.

exercises.english: When the theatre was sold out, we watched a film instead.
exercises.german: Als das Theater ausverkauft war, sahen wir uns stattdessen einen Film an.
exercises.why: als for a one-off past situation; a separable verb closes the clause, its prefix rejoins the main clause.

exercises.english: If you would like an appointment, feel free to call me back.
exercises.german: Falls Sie einen Termin wünschen, rufen Sie mich gern zurück.
exercises.why: wünschen is a formal main-clause verb in position II, the clause verb wünschen is repeated as the condition itself.

exercises.english: Once you live in Berlin, you get to know the city quickly.
exercises.german: Wenn man einmal in Berlin wohnt, lernt man die Stadt schnell kennen.
exercises.why: einmal … then generalises; the two clauses share the impersonal subject man and a separable verb in the clause.

exercises.english: When I had finished the book, I wanted to recommend it right away.
exercises.german: Als ich das Buch zu Ende gelesen hatte, wollte ich es sofort weiterempfehlen.
exercises.why: Plusquamperfekt gelesen hatte closes the als-clause, marking the earlier of two past moments.

exercises.english: If he comes next time, he pays the bill.
exercises.german: Wenn er das nächste Mal kommt, zahlt er die Rechnung.
exercises.why: Simple present in the clause stands for a future event; the main clause uses Präteritum for the consequence.

exercises.english: If you do not like it, we will exchange it.
exercises.german: Falls es dir nicht gefällt, tauschen wir es um.
exercises.why: Negated clause verb gefällt plus a separable verb in the main clause whose prefix um- goes to the end.

exercises.english: When I was small, I was allowed to stay up later.
exercises.german: Als ich klein war, durfte ich abends länger wach bleiben.
exercises.why: Modal durfte with an infinitive in the main clause; the state clause war is the short closing verb.

exercises.english: If you write to me, I will reply immediately.
exercises.german: Wenn Sie mir schreiben, antworte ich sofort.
exercises.why: A dative object in the clause sits before the final verb; the main clause has its verb in position II.

exercises.english: If it rains, we will have a picnic in the garden.
exercises.german: Falls es regnet, machen wir ein Picknick im Garten.
exercises.why: Akkusativ ein Picknick as the accusative object; nehmen/machen keeps the prefix in position III.

exercises.english: When my grandmother turned 90, all the neighbours came.
exercises.german: Als meine Großmutter 90 Jahre alt wurde, kamen alle aus der Nachbarschaft.
exercises.why: als plus a temporal main clause; the elliptical alle aus der Nachbarschaft omits a verb on purpose.

exercises.english: If you read the instructions twice, you understand the steps.
exercises.german: Wenn man die Anleitung zweimal liest, versteht man die Schritte.
exercises.why: Non-finite liest is the clause verb; the main clause repeats man so the impersonal reading stays clear.

exercises.english: If you fill in the form incorrectly, the application will be rejected.
exercises.german: Falls ihr das Formular falsch ausfüllt, wird der Antrag abgelehnt.
exercises.why: Passiv in the main clause (wird … abgelehnt) with the finite wird in position II and the prefix at the end.

exercises.english: When we were last in the city, everything was much quieter.
exercises.german: Als wir das letzte Mal in der Stadt waren, war alles viel ruhiger.
exercises.why: das letzte Mal als stands for the last occurrence; war is a short state verb that stays last in the clause.

exercises.english: If the weather holds, we will go on a bike tour.
exercises.german: Wenn das Wetter hält, machen wir eine Radtour.
exercises.why: A condition in the present with a planned main clause; hält is the finite clause verb.

exercises.english: If you have questions, just ask me!
exercises.german: Falls du Fragen hast, frag mich einfach!
exercises.why: Informal imperative in the main clause; the exclamation mark and the enclitic mich follow the imperative word.

exercises.english: If I had more time, I would take a course.
exercises.german: Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, würde ich einen Kurs belegen.
exercises.why: Unreal condition: hätte in the clause, würde plus infinitive in the main clause.

exercises.english: In your place I would accept the offer immediately.
exercises.german: An deiner Stelle würde ich das Angebot sofort annehmen.
exercises.why: würde in position II with a separable verb: the prefix annahm- returns as annehmen at the end.

exercises.english: Had I known, I would have come.
exercises.german: Hätte ich davon gewusst, wäre ich gekommen.
exercises.why: Wäre plus a participle clause replaces wenn; the Konjunktiv II condition stands first without wenn.

exercises.english: If it were not raining, we could eat outside.
exercises.german: Wenn es nicht regnete, könnten wir draußen essen.
exercises.why: regnete is Konjunktiv II of regnen for the unreal present; the negated regnete inverts nothing in the clause.

exercises.english: I would read longer in the evenings if I were not so tired.
exercises.german: Ich würde abends länger lesen, wenn ich nicht so müde wäre.
exercises.why: The unreal condition follows the main clause here, and the clause closes with wäre.

exercises.english: If I had no visa, I would cancel the trip.
exercises.german: Wenn ich kein Visum hätte, würde ich die Reise absagen.
exercises.why: Negated condition mit kein Visum; hätte closes the clause, absagen follows würde in the main clause.

exercises.english: If you were right, I would apologise.
exercises.german: Wenn du recht hättest, würde ich mich entschuldigen.
exercises.why: hättest in the informal second person; the main clause uses a reflexive pronoun before the infinitive.

exercises.english: If my sister came today, I would go out to eat with her.
exercises.german: Käme meine Schwester heute, ginge ich mit ihr essen.
exercises.why: Two different Konjunktiv II forms, käme and ginge, with keine inversion after the fronted condition.

exercises.english: If we had known, we would have reacted differently.
exercises.german: Hätten wir das gewusst, hätten wir anders reagiert.
exercises.why: Konjunktiv II plus Perfect (hätten … gewusst) for an unreal past condition, with würde deliberately avoided.

exercises.english: I would have to sleep more if I wanted to pass the exam.
exercises.german: Ich müsste mehr schlafen, wenn ich die Prüfung schaffen wollte.
exercises.why: Two modal Konjunktiv II forms, müsste and wollte, with the infinitives at the end of each clause.

exercises.english: If you had asked me, I would have helped you.
exercises.german: Wenn du mich gefragt hättest, hätte ich dir geholfen.
exercises.why: Plusquamperfekt in the clause and a modal-style hätte in the main clause; the object dir sits before geholfen.

exercises.english: If I had time, I would love to come along.
exercises.german: Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich zu gern mitkommen.
exercises.why: The degree adverb zu gern modifies the whole main clause; the clause still ends with hätte.

exercises.english: Without a driving licence I would not be allowed to drive the vehicle.
exercises.german: Ohne einen Führerschein dürfte ich das Fahrzeug nicht fahren.
exercises.why: dürfte is the Konjunktiv II of dürfen and expresses hypothetical permission here, not real authorisation.

exercises.english: If I were rich, I would travel around the world.
exercises.german: Wäre ich reich, würde ich um die Welt reisen.
exercises.why: Fronted wären-clause with the finite verb first; the main clause has a prepositional object um die Welt.

exercises.english: If we had started earlier, everything would be finished.
exercises.german: Würden wir früher angefangen haben, wäre alles fertig.
exercises.why: Mixed unreal condition: Konjunktiv II Perfect in the clause against a result in the Konjunktiv II of sein.

exercises.english: He would help me if I asked him to.
exercises.german: Er würde mir helfen, wenn ich ihn darum bäte.
exercises.why: bäte is the Konjunktiv II of bitten, a strong verb, and closes the clause without an auxiliary.

exercises.english: What would happen if the power went out?
exercises.german: Was würde passieren, wenn der Strom ausfiele?
exercises.why: A w-question in position I plus an indirect question with the Konjunktiv II form ausfiele at the end.

exercises.english: Without her promise I would not have taken on the project.
exercises.german: Ohne ihr Zusage hätte ich das Projekt nicht übernommen.
exercises.why: A prepositional phrase replaces the wenn-clause; the main clause uses the Konjunktiv II of the perfect.

exercises.english: If I had not passed the exam, I would change the subject.
exercises.german: Wenn ich die Prüfung nicht bestanden hätte, würde ich das Fach wechseln.
exercises.why: A negated Konjunktiv II perfect in the clause; the negated main clause still keeps würde in position II.

exercises.english: If the offer had been higher, I would have accepted it.
exercises.german: Wäre das Angebot höher gewesen, hätte ich es angenommen.
exercises.why: Konjunktiv II of sein as the auxiliary for a past state, plus a modal hätte with a participle in the main clause.

exercises.english: He says that he is in Berlin right now.
exercises.german: Er sagt, er sei gerade in Berlin.
exercises.why: Reported present: indicative bin becomes Konjunktiv I sei, and the reported clause goes verb-final.

exercises.english: She claims that she never received the email.
exercises.german: Sie behauptet, sie habe die E-Mail nie bekommen.
exercises.why: Reported past: habe instead of hat, with the participle bekommen standing behind the object.

exercises.english: The colleague says that he will be punctual today.
exercises.german: Der Kollege meint, er komme heute pünktlich.
exercises.why: komme is the Konjunktiv I of kommen, used to report a future statement without adding a frame verb.

exercises.english: I have heard that the meeting has been cancelled.
exercises.german: Ich habe gehört, das Meeting sei abgesagt worden.
exercises.why: Reported passive in the perfect: sei plus a double participle, with worden as the finite-verb slot.

exercises.english: She says that she has a cold.
exercises.german: Sie sagt, sie sei erkältet.
exercises.why: A state rather than an action, so the Konjunktiv I of sein carries the report; no tense shift needed.

exercises.english: The doctor says that he will operate on the patient tomorrow.
exercises.german: Der Arzt sagt, er werde die Patientin morgen operieren.
exercises.why: werde reports the doctor as the subject of the future clause; operieren is the accusative infinitive at the end.

exercises.english: The newspaper reports that the minister has announced his resignation.
exercises.german: Die Zeitung berichtet, der Minister habe den Rücktritt angekündigt.
exercises.why: Perfect in the reported clause: habe plus angekündigt, with the accusative object in front of the verb.

exercises.english: He means that this is his only chance.
exercises.german: Er meint, das sei seine einzige Möglichkeit.
exercises.why: The demonstrative das is left at the front and sei closes the clause; a possesive pronoun follows it.

exercises.english: She says that she did not know.
exercises.german: Sie sagt, sie habe es nicht gewusst.
exercises.why: Reported past: the negated Konjunktiv I perfect habe … gewusst is not replaced by the Konjunktiv II.

exercises.english: The customer claims that he did not order anything.
exercises.german: Der Kunde behauptet, er habe nichts bestellt.
exercises.why: habe plus a negated accusative object, with the personal pronoun er as the reported subject.

exercises.english: The author explains that the book appeared in 1998.
exercises.german: Die Autorin erklärt, das Buch sei 1998 erschienen.
exercises.why: Reported past as a Konjunktiv I perfect of appear; the date interrupts between subject and participle.

exercises.english: He asks whether I have time.
exercises.german: Er fragt, ob ich Zeit habe.
exercises.why: Konjunktiv I in an ob-clause: habe takes the place of the original habe, keeping verb-final order.

exercises.skill: Conditional: indirect ob-question with Konjunktiv I
exercises.english: The doctor asks whether she tolerates the medicine.
exercises.german: Der Arzt fragt, ob sie das Medikament vertrage.
exercises.why: vertrage is the Konjunktiv I of vertragen and closes the indirect question after the subject.

exercises.english: The coach says that the team is playing better.
exercises.german: Der Trainer sagt, die Mannschaft spiele besser.
exercises.why: spiele shows the e-change of the Konjunktiv I, while the comparative besser is the second part of the predicate.

exercises.english: She writes that she is stuck in traffic.
exercises.german: Sie schreibt, sie sei im Stau.
exercises.why: Konjunktiv I sei in a report triggered by schreiben; the prepositional phrase stays before the verb.

exercises.english: He claims that he did not accept the order.
exercises.german: Er behauptet, er habe den Auftrag nicht angenommen.
exercises.why: A separable verb in the reported perfect: angenommen ends the clause, the prefix is split off.

exercises.english: My sister thinks that the film is boring.
exercises.german: Meine Schwester meint, der Film sei langweilig.
exercises.why: A predicative adjective takes the Konjunktiv I of sein, so the reported clause ends in sei.

exercises.english: The boss says that he will inform us tomorrow.
exercises.german: Der Chef sagt, er werde uns morgen informieren.
exercises.why: werde plus accusative uns; the date sits between the subject and the infinitive inside the clause.

exercises.english: She wrote that the train was delayed.
exercises.german: Sie schrieb, der Zug habe sich verspätet.
exercises.why: Konjunktiv I perfect with a reflexive verb: habe plus a participle whose prefix sitz- is in the middle.

exercises.english: He says that the price will not change.
exercises.german: Er sagt, der Preis werde sich nicht ändern.
exercises.why: A reported future: werde plus a reflexive verb, with the negation in front of the final infinitive.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: I get up early in order to catch the train.
exercises.german: Ich stehe früh auf, um den Zug zu erreichen.
exercises.why: um … zu with the same subject in both parts; the main-clause verb is finite, not a modal, as um … zu requires.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: She phoned in order to arrange an appointment.
exercises.german: Sie telefonierte, um einen Termin zu vereinbaren.
exercises.why: Präteritum main-clause verb plus an accusative-infinitive purpose clause in um … zu.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: He often calculates in order to check the sum.
exercises.german: Er rechnet oft, um die Summe zu prüfen.
exercises.why: The purpose infinitive zu prüfen follows um, and rechnen stays finite in position II.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: We save money in order to be able to travel in summer.
exercises.german: Wir sparen, um im Sommer verreisen zu können.
exercises.why: The modal-like können sits inside the zu-infinitive; the main clause verb sparen is still finite, which um … zu allows.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: I write it on the board in order that everyone can read it.
exercises.german: Ich schreibe es an die Tafel, damit alle es lesen können.
exercises.why: damit introduces a purpose clause with a modal, which rules out um … zu with the same subject.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: The trainer explains the exercises so that the students understand them.
exercises.german: Der Trainer erklärt die Übungen, damit die Schüler sie verstehen.
exercises.why: damit with a different subject in each clause; the pronoun sie in the purpose clause points back to die Übungen.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: I am sending you the file so that you can check it.
exercises.german: Ich schicke dir die Datei, damit du sie prüfen kannst.
exercises.why: Modal kannst in the purpose clause goes after the infinitive at the very end, unlike Konjunktiv I word order.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: Please speak more slowly so that I understand you.
exercises.german: Sprich bitte langsamer, damit ich dich verstehe.
exercises.why: An imperative main clause followed by damit, where the Konjunktiv I verstehe is the normal reported form.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: She sets an alarm so that you do not miss the departure.
exercises.german: Sie stellt einen Wecker, damit ihr die Abfahrt nicht entgeht.
exercises.why: A dative object in the purpose clause and a reflexive verb whose prefix ent- is split off at the end.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: The interpreter switches language so that all the guests can follow.
exercises.german: Der Dolmetscher wechselt die Sprache, damit alle Gäste folgen können.
exercises.why: A separable verb in both halves: wechselt closes nothing, the prefix stays in position III, and folgen können closes the clause.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: We practise every day so that the grade at the end is better.
exercises.german: Wir üben jeden Tag, damit die Note am Ende besser ist.
exercises.why: damit states a goal, so a Konjunktiv I ist is used rather than a bare indicative.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: It rained so hard that the streets were flooded.
exercises.german: Es regnete so stark, dass die Straßen überflutet waren.
exercises.why: so + degree + dass states a result; waren is Präteritum of sein, and überflutet is the participle in the clause.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: He spoke so quietly that I could barely understand him.
exercises.german: Er sprach so leise, dass ich ihn kaum verstehen konnte.
exercises.why: so leise plus dass and a Präteritum modal in the result clause, which follows the main clause.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: The child was so tired that she fell asleep immediately.
exercises.german: Das Kind war so müde, dass es sofort einschlief.
exercises.why: A result clause with a separable verb: the prefix ein- is in the middle and the verb schlief ends the clause.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: The meeting lasted so long that everybody got hungry.
exercises.german: Die Besprechung dauerte so lange, dass alle hungrig wurden.
exercises.why: so + adjective-like lange introduces the degree; wurden is the simple past of werden in the result clause.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: She talked so fast that nobody could follow.
exercises.german: Sie redete so schnell, dass niemand mitkam.
exercises.why: The result clause uses a simple past verb rather than a modal, and mit- stays attached to kam.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: It was so cold that we stayed indoors.
exercises.german: Es war so kalt, dass wir drinnen blieben.
exercises.why: war is the Konjunktiv II of sein but reads as simple past; so kalt plus dass makes the degree explicit.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: The mountain was so steep that we had to turn back.
exercises.german: Der Berg war so steil, dass wir umkehren mussten.
exercises.why: A modal in the result clause plus an accusative-infinitive (umkehren), which dass-clauses can contain.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: The music was so loud that I could not concentrate.
exercises.german: Die Musik war so laut, dass ich mich nicht konzentrieren konnte.
exercises.why: A reflexive pronoun in the result clause before the negative particle and the final modal.

exercises.skill: Purpose and result: damit / um zu / sodass
exercises.english: He translated so badly that the meaning was lost.
exercises.german: Er übersetzte so schlecht, dass der Sinn verloren ging.
exercises.why: So schlecht plus dass expresses a negative degree; the result clause is passive in meaning without a modal.

exercises.english: Only whoever knows the deadline can judge the date.
exercises.german: Nur wer die Frist kennt, kann den Termin beurteilen.
exercises.why: Nur before a free relative clause restricts the group; the free relative keeps verb-final order (kennt).

exercises.english: I have only read half of the article.
exercises.german: Ich habe nur die Hälfte des Artikels gelesen.
exercises.why: nur modifies the quantity, and the negated implicit alternative is what makes the sentence restrictive.

exercises.english: Only the neighbours heard the noise.
exercises.german: Bloß die Nachbarn haben den Lärm gehört.
exercises.why: bloß is the colloquial equivalent of nur and stands in position I before the subject.

exercises.english: Employees who arrive late lose their bonus.
exercises.german: Mitarbeiter, die zu spät kommen, verlieren ihren Bonus.
exercises.why: A defining relative clause without a comma: it identifies which employees are meant, so the sentence is restrictive.

exercises.english: Only if you hurry will we catch the train.
exercises.german: Nur wenn du dich beeilst, schaffen wir den Zug.
exercises.why: Nur wenn restricts the condition itself; the main clause is positive, which is required after this restrictive form.

exercises.english: Only a few listeners were sitting in the hall.
exercises.german: Im Saal saßen nur wenige Zuhörer.
exercises.why: A fronted prepositional phrase puts the verb in position III, and nur restricts wenige to a small number.

exercises.english: The town where I grew up lies in the south of the country.
exercises.german: Die Stadt, in der ich aufwuchs, liegt im Süden des Landes.
exercises.why: A prepositional relative clause in der ich aufwuchs; aufwuchs is the Konjunktiv I of aufwachsen and ends the clause.

exercises.english: The book that my brother lent me is still here.
exercises.german: Das Buch, das mir mein Bruder geliehen hat, liegt noch hier.
exercises.why: A dative relative pronoun das because the book is the recipient's object; geliehen hat closes the relative clause.

exercises.english: Just do not take the seven o'clock train!
exercises.german: Nimm bloß nicht den Zug um sieben!
exercises.why: bloß before a negative imperative intensifies the warning; the accusative article follows negated nicht.

exercises.english: Only one single candidate passed the exam.
exercises.german: Nur ein einziger Kandidat hat die Prüfung bestanden.
exercises.why: Nur and ein einziger both restrict the number; the relative position of the subject is not needed here.

exercises.english: Everyone who applied will receive a written reply.
exercises.german: Alle, die sich beworben haben, bekommen eine schriftliche Antwort.
exercises.why: A free relative clause after plural-alle restricts them to the applicants; the Perfect closes the clause.

exercises.english: The colleague with whom I lead the project is on holiday this week.
exercises.german: Der Kollege, mit dem ich das Projekt leite, ist diese Woche im Urlaub.
exercises.why: A prepositional relative clause with dem, which stands for the colleague; the defining relative takes no second comma.

exercises.english: I only called briefly.
exercises.german: Ich habe bloß kurz angerufen.
exercises.why: bloß restricts the manner (kurz) and rules out every other degree of effort, not just the time.

exercises.english: Part-time staff who have worked for more than two years get a bonus.
exercises.german: Teilzeitkräfte, die länger als zwei Jahre arbeiten, erhalten einen Zuschlag.
exercises.why: The relative clause selects exactly those employees who qualify; länger als needs no comma after the relative pronoun.

exercises.english: Only for that reason did we reject the offer.
exercises.german: Nur deshalb haben wir das Angebot abgelehnt.
exercises.why: Nur deshalb as the focus at the front; the Perfect uses the prefixed form of abgelehnt after the subject.

exercises.english: That was just a harmless mistake.
exercises.german: Das war bloß ein harmloser Irrtum.
exercises.why: bloß dismisses the significance, and war is the finite verb in position II of a very short main clause.

exercises.english: Children whose parents both work get a hot meal with us.
exercises.german: Kinder, deren Eltern beide arbeiten, bekommen bei uns ein warmes Essen.
exercises.why: A genitive relative clause with deren; the defining relative clause is the reason for the benefit described.

exercises.english: I simply cannot find a suitable flat.
exercises.german: Ich finde bloß keine passende Wohnung.
exercises.why: bloß plus a negated accusative object, expressing that no suitable flat at all can be found.

exercises.english: You will only get an appointment with a referral.
exercises.german: Nur mit einer Empfehlung bekommen Sie einen Termin.
exercises.why: Nur mit plus a formal Sie main clause; mit einer Empfehlung is the restricted condition for the appointment.

exercises.english: Whoever applies early has clearly better chances.
exercises.german: Wer sich früh bewirbt, hat deutlich bessere Chancen.
exercises.why: A free relative clause as the subject in nominative; the whole sentence generalises, so there is no antecedent to restrict.
